title: Aphorism § 101
text:
§ 101



 It may easily happen that in the first case of an epidemic disease
          that presents itself to the physician's notice he does not at once obtain a knowledge of
          its complete picture, as it is only by a close observation of several cases of every such
          collective disease that he can become conversant with the totality of its signs and
          symptoms. The carefully observing physician can, however, from the examination of even the
          first and second patients, often arrive so nearly at a knowledge of the true state as to
          have in his mind a characteristic portrait of it, and even to succeed in finding a
          suitable, homoeopathically adapted remedy for it.
